main_text.p: in quibufdam literas σ, præponunt; ut ἐρύβ&, ρεύβ&, &c.

'Οἰχάζω, fimplex; ex quo compositum ἐνοχάζω, quod exponit Hefychius, τὰ παιδία ἢ χερσὶν ἀνασείειν, infantes manibus certo ritu agitare, vel quatere: de quo ritu plura viri docti ad Perfii, Tunc manibus quatit, &c. to rock, cunas agitare.

'Οὔλω, folum, pavimentum, terra. Anglis, threshold, eft limen domus: quod compositum reor, ex Ἰσθ, (Anglice, ex Græco, θύρα:) & ἔδαφος: q.d. pavimentum januæ. Eft enim pars inferior januæ, folo proxima; fuperliminari oppofita.

Οὔρῳ, (vox Homero familiaris; pro quâ pofteriores φυλάσσω maluerunt:) cuftos: ἀρέω (ex alia tamen hoc origine:) curare, cuftodire. Anglis, ward, warden; cuftos, quod etiam, ward, &c. Olim waren, cuftodire, de quo Notæ ad Williramum, p.11. Item hodiernum warie, cautus, fedulus, follicitus. Item, to beware, cavere, præcavere.

page.notes: Black letter and Greek words are approximated; several Greek and Old English words are doubtful, especially in the glosses on lines 1, 4, 5 and 6 of the paragraphs. The bottom line is partly cut off at the foot.
